gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each 4-channel pick costs on 2026-11-21 once its parking-mode hardwire kit is added: the Redtiger F17 Plus comes to $225.98 and the Rexing C4 to $229.98 ($249.97 with its GPS adapter), both from the makers' stores.
standout_why: Compared against cartechtalk.com, deal.ai, gearjury.com and wikidashcam.org. cartechtalk gives undated prices and no kit price; deal.ai gives retailer prices with no kit information; gearjury and wikidashcam give no prices at all. None prices the Rexing C4, Redtiger F17 Plus or a hardwire kit. Tom's Guide came back truncated and Car and Driver could not be fetched, so the two pages ChatGPT cited most are not compared. Our own best-4-channel page already carries today's C4, F17 Plus and N5S prices but no kit prices. Kept at 2 because the Botslab and LAMTTO kit facts were not read from the makers' pages (rate-limited).
decides: It answers the caveat ChatGPT itself raised ('provided its parking-mode hardware fits within your $250 total budget'). The F17 Plus and C4 both stay under $250 with a maker kit added; the C4 has only $0.03 to spare once its GPS adapter is included. The Vantrue N5S ($293.99) and Rexing R4 ($259.99) are over the line before any kit. The Botslab G980H 4-camera stays the linkable pick at $192.70 through our link (store price $234.99), which leaves $57.30 for a kit, but whether a kit is in the box, and its price, must be read from botslab.com before the page asserts an all-in figure.
